# Add Target Language Translations

## Plan Metadata

- **Revision:** 3
- **Status:** Approved
- **Roadmap item:** Target languages and translations
- **Last revised:** 2026-10-26
- **Requirements:** the Language section of `../requirements.md`
- **Feature lists:** `frontend/docs/features.md`
- **Code style:** `../code-style.md`
- **Approval record:** The user asked for Revision 3 to be implemented on 2026-10-26.

## Outcome And Acceptance

A Home Assistant user whose language is a target language sees SAJ Local's integration texts, card texts and documentation in that language. The target languages, from the Language section of `../requirements.md`, are German, Dutch, French, Simplified Chinese, Spanish, Italian, Polish and Swedish.

The work is accepted when:

1. `custom_components/saj_local/translations/` holds one file for each target language, named by the Home Assistant language code: `de.json`, `nl.json`, `fr.json`, `zh-Hans.json`, `es.json`, `it.json`, `pl.json` and `sv.json`. Each file has every key of `en.json`, with the same `{placeholder}` names in each text.
2. `frontend/src/i18n/` holds one file for each target language with the same names as item 1. Each file has every key of `frontend/src/i18n/en.json`, and the plural keys the language's plural rules use: Polish needs `_one`, `_few`, `_many` and `_other`, and Chinese needs `_other` only.
3. `docs/<code>/user/` and `docs/<code>/developer/` exist for each target language, with the lowercase codes `de`, `nl`, `fr`, `zh-hans`, `es`, `it`, `pl` and `sv`, and hold a translation of every page under `docs/en-gb/user/` and `docs/en-gb/developer/` under the same file name. `docs/<code>/user/entities/` is generated by `make docs` from the language's translation file. Every text a reader sees is translated: prose, headings, table cells, link texts (also links to the English feature lists and requirement documents), image and badge alt texts, link titles and the comments inside code blocks. Only code, keys, entity IDs, file paths, register addresses, model names, units and the simulator's English UI names stay English.
4. `docs/images/<code>/` holds every screenshot for each target language, taken by `make docs-images` from a Home Assistant whose user language is the target language.
5. `make docs-check` checks every language folder under `docs/`, and `make ci` passes.
6. The root `README.md` stays in English in the repository root. Each target language has a translation of it at `docs/<code>/README.md`, whose links point to the pages of that language (for example `user/README.md`) wherever the root `README.md` links a documentation page. The root `README.md` and every `docs/<code>/README.md` start with the language bar of item 11, where `en` stands for the root `README.md`. The list of language links in the root `README.md`'s documentation section is removed, because the bar replaces it.
7. The cards' entry under "Theme and language" in `frontend/docs/features.md`, the matching section of `docs/en-gb/user/cards/README.md`, the line on `src/i18n/` in `docs/en-gb/developer/frontend.md` and "Adding a second language" in `docs/en-gb/developer/documentation.md` describe the languages as built, and the translated pages say the same.
8. `custom_components/saj_local/docs/features.md` has a "Languages" section listing every language the integration ships. `custom_components/saj_local/docs/requirements.md` has a matching "Languages" section stating the translation needs without naming languages. The two sections link each other with `Requirements:` and `Features:` lines.
9. `docs/en-gb/user/nomenclature.md` lists every SAJ and Home Assistant term the integration, the cards and the documentation use, each with a one-line meaning, and `docs/<code>/user/nomenclature.md` holds the term and meaning in each target language. The user documentation index of each language links to its nomenclature page.
10. A test in `tests/saj-integration/test_translations.py` fails when any `translations/<code>.json` lacks a key of `en.json`, has a key `en.json` does not have, or uses different `{placeholder}` names in a text.
11. Every page under `docs/<code>/user/` and `docs/<code>/developer/`, in every language including `en-gb` and the generated entity pages, starts with a language bar as its first line, above the page title: `en | de | nl | fr | zh | es | it | pl | sv`, always in that order, with ` | ` between the labels. Each label except the current language links to the same page in that language's folder by a relative link; the current language's label is plain text, not a link. The labels map to the folders `en` → `en-gb`, `de` → `de`, `nl` → `nl`, `fr` → `fr`, `zh` → `zh-hans`, `es` → `es`, `it` → `it`, `pl` → `pl`, `sv` → `sv`.

## Existing Baseline

- **Integration.** Every user-facing text goes through Home Assistant's translation system, and the library's English error texts are converted to translation keys in `custom_components/saj_local/errors.py`. Home Assistant loads `translations/<code>.json` for the user's language. Log messages stay English.
- **Entity IDs.** SAJ Local sets every entity ID itself from the register key (`fixed_entity_id` in `custom_components/saj_local/entity.py`), so entity IDs stay `<type>.saj_<key>` in every language. Without the fixed ID, Home Assistant 2026.9.3 builds entity IDs from the translated name for German, Dutch, French, Spanish, Italian, Polish and Swedish (`NATIVE_ENTITY_IDS` in `homeassistant/generated/languages.py`, used by `EntityPlatform.async_load_translations`). No entity ID work is needed.
- **Cards.** `frontend/src/i18n/localize.ts` loads every `*.json` file in the folder, lowercases the file name, matches the user's language exactly and then by base language, and falls back to English. Plural keys use `Intl.PluralRules`. `frontend/tests/i18n/localize.test.ts` already requires one card file for each integration translation file and the same keys as English in every card file, so the integration and card files of a language land in the same change. Entity names, values and states come from Home Assistant's own formatting.
- **Documentation.** `docs/en-gb/developer/documentation.md` ("Adding a second language") already fixes the layout: sibling folders `docs/<locale>/` and `docs/images/<locale>/` with the same file names, and nothing moves.
- **Docs check and generator.** `.github/scripts/docs_check.py` reads only `docs/en-gb` (`DOCS_DIRECTORY`) and `en.json` (`TRANSLATIONS_FILE`). The generator's own texts are English strings in the script: the area titles and descriptions, the table header, the notes such as "Phase {n} and above", the equipment names and the generated notice.
- **Screenshots.** `frontend/tests/browser/docs/screenshots.spec.ts` takes the language from `DOCS_LOCALE` (default `en-GB`) and writes to `docs/images/<locale in lowercase>/`. `languageLabels` names only `en-GB`. The spec finds controls by English labels, both Home Assistant's labels (for example "Settings", "Close", "Configure", "Add integration") and SAJ Local's labels (for example "Host", "Prefix", "Add polling group"). `tests/playwright/run-docs-images.sh` runs the spec once for one language.
- **Copy-paste check.** `make copy-paste` runs jscpd over Markdown with a minimum of 5 lines and 50 tokens, and `docs/` is never excluded. The English docs have six code blocks of five lines or more: four in `developer/simulator.md`, one in `developer/simulator-page.md` and one in `user/cards/power-flow-card.md`. A code block copied unchanged into eight more languages would be reported as duplicated.

## Boundaries And Decisions

- The translations are written by the implementing agent, like any other implementation work.
- Each language uses one term for one thing across the integration, the cards and the documentation, as recorded in the language's `nomenclature.md`. SAJ terms follow SAJ's own wording on SAJ's website in that language (for example `de.saj-electric.com/de-de`, `nl` at `www.saj-electric.com/nl-nl`, `zh-cn` at `www.saj-electric.com/zh-cn`). Home Assistant terms follow Home Assistant's own translation for that language.
- Keys, entity IDs, placeholder names, units, register addresses, model names (HS3, H2) and code stay as they are in English.
- Translated documentation keeps the tone and the structure of the English page: the same headings in the same order, the same links, the same screenshots by file name.
- The feature lists and the requirement documents stay English only. Translated pages link to the English feature list sections by the same heading anchors as the English pages.
- `manifest.json` keeps the English documentation URL, because Home Assistant takes one URL.
- The simulator pages under `mock/static/` stay English only. The translated developer pages describe the English simulator page.
- No check is added to keep the languages in step with English. Each later change to an English text, page or screenshot updates every language in the same change.

## Phases

### Phase 1 — Integration texts

Phases 1 and 2 land in one change, because of the card test named under "Existing Baseline".

1. Write `docs/en-gb/user/nomenclature.md` (item 9 of "Outcome And Acceptance") and its translation into `docs/<code>/user/nomenclature.md` for each target language, before any other translation. Every later translation in every phase uses the terms of the language's nomenclature page. Link the English page from `docs/en-gb/user/README.md`.
2. Write `custom_components/saj_local/translations/<code>.json` for each target language from `en.json`.
3. Add the test of item 10 of "Outcome And Acceptance" to `tests/saj-integration/test_translations.py`.
4. Add the "Languages" sections of item 8 of "Outcome And Acceptance" to `custom_components/saj_local/docs/features.md` and `custom_components/saj_local/docs/requirements.md`.
5. Smoke check in the development Home Assistant: the full smoke check (the config flow, the options flow, a repair issue, an entity list and an error message) runs in English only. For each target language, one very small check with the user language set to that language confirms that SAJ Local's texts actually show translated, for example one entity name and the config flow title.

### Phase 2 — Card texts

1. Write `frontend/src/i18n/<code>.json` for each target language from `frontend/src/i18n/en.json`, with the plural keys of item 2 of "Outcome And Acceptance".
2. Change the test "gives every language the same keys as English" in `frontend/tests/i18n/localize.test.ts`: every language has every key of English, except that a plural key has exactly the forms the language's `Intl.PluralRules` categories list. The test as written demands English's `_one` and `_other` only, so a Polish file with `_few` and `_many` fails, and a Polish file without the forms shows the bare key for a count of 2.
3. Update "Theme and language" in `frontend/docs/features.md`: the cards' own texts exist in English and every target language, and other languages show the cards' texts in English.
4. Rebuild the card bundle with `make build`.

### Phase 3 — Docs check and generator for every language

1. `docs_check.py` runs every rule on each folder `docs/<code>/` that exists, and the orphan image rule on each `docs/images/<code>/` against the pages of the same language.
2. The Feature Coverage Table stays only in `docs/en-gb/developer/documentation.md`. `docs-check` applies the table to every language folder under the same page names.
3. The generator writes `docs/<code>/user/entities/` from the matching translation file: `en-gb` from `en.json`, `zh-hans` from `zh-Hans.json`, and so on.
4. The generator takes the equipment names (today's `EQUIPMENT_TITLES`) from the equipment selector options of the language's `translations/<code>.json`, so the entity pages and the config flow use the same term. `EQUIPMENT_TITLES` is removed from the script.
5. The generator's other own texts, the ones the integration translation file does not have (the area titles and descriptions, the table header, the notes such as "Phase {n} and above" and the generated notice), move out of the script into one JSON file for each language under `.github/scripts/docs_text/`, named by the lowercase docs code (`en-gb.json`, `de.json` and so on). The English file holds today's texts unchanged.
6. Unit tests in `tests/scripts/` cover the language folder discovery, the per-language generation, the equipment names taken from the translation file and the per-language orphan image rule, keeping the 100 % coverage gate.

### Phase 4 — Screenshots for every language

The spec finds nothing by a hand-written label, in any language including English. No label table exists in the spec.

1. The spec sets the user language by the language code (`de`, `zh-Hans` and so on), not by the label the language picker shows. `languageLabels` is removed.
2. The spec opens every Home Assistant screen it needs by its URL route (for example `/config/integrations/integration/saj_local`) instead of clicking through menus by label.
3. The spec finds SAJ Local's form fields by the `name` attribute Home Assistant gives each field from the schema key (`host`, `prefix` and so on), and the cards by their own elements and attributes.
4. The spec finds Home Assistant's own controls by language-independent selectors (element, role and attribute). A Home Assistant control that has only its text, such as a dialog's Close button, is found by its text read at run time from the running Home Assistant with `hass.localize("<key>")`, for example `hass.localize("ui.common.close")`, so the text always matches the running version and language. A Home Assistant key rename breaks every language at once and is fixed in one place in the spec.
5. `tests/playwright/run-docs-images.sh` runs the spec once for each language, English first, with fresh containers each run. `ARGS` selects one language by code. Update the `docs-images` help in `.github/scripts/check_steps.py` and the Screenshots section of `docs/en-gb/developer/documentation.md`.
6. Run `make docs-images` and review the images of every language.

### Phase 5 — Translate the documentation

Phase 5 lands as one change covering every target language.

1. Every code block stays inline on its page, in every language including English. The shared example files under `docs/examples/` are moved back into the pages that link them, `docs/examples/` is removed, and the `docs-check` rule on shared example files and its unit tests are removed. Each fenced code block that the copy-paste check reports as duplicated across languages is wrapped in a `<!-- jscpd:ignore-start -->` and `<!-- jscpd:ignore-end -->` marker pair, in every language's copy of the page, under the exception in "Copy-paste exceptions" below. A marker pair wraps one code block and nothing else.
2. Translate every page under `docs/en-gb/user/` and `docs/en-gb/developer/` into `docs/<code>/` for each target language, user pages first, using the terms of the language's `nomenclature.md`, translating every text named in item 3 of "Outcome And Acceptance". Each page links to the screenshots in `docs/images/<code>/`. The two Home Assistant badges in `user/installation.md` carry translated alt text, so the badge lines differ by language. The test-folder table in `developer/checks.md` holds only folder paths, so the translated `developer/checks.md` links to the table on the English page by its heading anchor instead of holding a copy, as the Feature Coverage Table does. If `make copy-paste` reports any duplicate outside a marker pair of item 1, stop and ask the user.
3. Rewrite "Adding a second language" in `docs/en-gb/developer/documentation.md` as "Languages", describing the layout, the generator, the screenshot runs, the marker pairs around duplicated code blocks and the rule that a change to English updates every language in the same change. Update the cards README and `developer/frontend.md` lines named in item 7 of "Outcome And Acceptance".
4. Write `docs/<code>/README.md` for each target language as item 6 of "Outcome And Acceptance" says, translating every visible text as item 3 says, and remove the language link list from the root `README.md`. The language bar of item 5 covers the root `README.md` and every `docs/<code>/README.md`: on the root `README.md` the `en` label is plain text and each other label links to `docs/<code>/README.md`; on `docs/<code>/README.md` the `en` label links to the root `README.md` and each other label to the README of that language.
5. The language bar of item 11 of "Outcome And Acceptance" is written by `make docs`, not by hand: the generator writes or replaces the bar on the first line of every page of every language folder, and on the generated entity pages as it writes them. The label order and the label-to-folder map live once in the generator. `docs-check` reports a page whose first line is not the expected bar, and a bar link to a page that does not exist. Unit tests in `tests/scripts/` cover writing, replacing and checking the bar, keeping the 100 % coverage gate. The "Languages" section of `docs/en-gb/developer/documentation.md` and of each translated `documentation.md` describes the bar and that `make docs` writes the bar.
6. Run `make docs` and `make ci`.

### Copy-paste exceptions

The rule in `AGENTS.md` allows a `jscpd:ignore-start` and `jscpd:ignore-end` marker pair only for a case the user wrote into a plan and approved. The user approved exactly one case for this plan (user, 2026-10-26):

- A fenced code block on a page under `docs/<code>/user/` or `docs/<code>/developer/`, in any language including `en-gb`, that is the same code as the matching block on the same page in another language. Translated comments inside the block do not remove the exception.

No other passage gets a marker pair: tables, badges, links and prose are made to differ by translation or are linked, as Phase 5 item 2 says.

## Verification Strategy

- `make ci` passes, including `docs-check`, `copy-paste`, `prettier` and `validate`.
- `make docs-images` passes for every language.
- The smoke checks of Phase 1 pass in the development Home Assistant: the full check in English and the small translated-text check in each target language.
- The test of item 10 of "Outcome And Acceptance" passes for every integration translation file.
- A dashboard with every SAJ Local card, viewed with the user language set to each target language, shows no English card text.

## Risks And Guardrails

- A Home Assistant version bump can rename a URL route, a selector or a translation key the screenshot spec uses. The break shows in every language at once and is fixed in one place in the spec.
- Machine-quality wording in a language is found by users. The beta testers of each language are asked to report wording.

## Settled Decisions

- Code blocks stay inline on every page; a code block duplicated across languages is wrapped in a jscpd ignore marker pair under the one exception in "Copy-paste exceptions", and `docs/examples/` is not used (user, 2026-10-26).
- Every visible text of a translated page is translated, including link texts, alt texts, link titles and code comments (user, 2026-10-26).
- Every documentation page starts with a language bar linking the same page in every language, in one fixed order, with the current language as plain text (user, 2026-10-26).
- The root `README.md` stays in the repository root in English; its translations live at `docs/<code>/README.md`, and all ten READMEs carry the language bar (user, 2026-10-26).
- The target languages are the eight of SAJ's website languages with the most Home Assistant installations (user, 2026-10-26).
- The scope covers the integration, the cards and the user and developer documentation. The feature lists and the requirement documents are internal and stay English (user, 2026-10-26).
- An agent translates, like any other implementation (user, 2026-10-26).
- Screenshots are taken again in every language (user, 2026-10-26).
- No check keeps languages in step with English (user, 2026-10-26).
- A pytest checks that every integration translation file has the keys and placeholder names of `en.json`, like the existing card test (user, 2026-10-26).
- The integration `features.md` lists every language shipped; the integration `requirements.md` states the translation needs without naming languages (user, 2026-10-26).
- The screenshot spec uses URL routes and selectors, and `hass.localize` for text-only Home Assistant controls, with no hand-kept label table (user, 2026-10-26).
- The generator takes equipment names from the integration translation file (user, 2026-10-26).
- Each language has a translated `docs/<code>/user/nomenclature.md`, written first in Phase 1 and followed by every later translation (user, 2026-10-26).
- A copy-paste duplicate outside an approved marker pair stops the work and goes to the user (user, 2026-10-26).
- Phase 5 lands as one change (user, 2026-10-26).
- The full smoke check runs in English only; each target language gets a very small check that its texts actually show translated (user, 2026-10-26).
